newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin asks banks to do more relending.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin asks banks to do more relending.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday that foreign bank offshore units operating in the Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF) should focus more on out-out lending activities.
Amnuay said loans brought in from abroad since the BIBF was established in 1993 were high and could help Thailand to become a financial centre in this region.
But the out-out business, especially to Thailand's neighbouring countries, was still not active, he said.
Amnuay's comments were made as he officially presented new BIBF operation licences to seven foreign banks.

The seven banks include Japan's Fuji Bank and the Tokai Bank, the Korea Development Bank KR006651526=, Generale Bank of Belgium, National Australia Bank, Union Bank of Switzerland and the Royal Bank of Canada.
Out-out loans are foreign funds brought in for processing by Thai-based banks for relending to borrowers in third countries.
